preamble: Insertion of [g] before a word-initial labio-velar glide [w]. In many rural and popular varieties of Spanish, a velar stop is inserted before initial [w], so huevo 'egg' is pronounced [ˈɡwe.β̞o], written güevo in eye-dialect spelling, and hueso 'bone' becomes güeso. The glide's velar constriction is strengthened into a full stop.

examples.note: Dialectal velar prothesis before the initial glide, written ⟨gü⟩ in eye-dialect spelling. The from form is the standard pronunciation, which keeps the conservative glide onset.
Listed by Wiktionary as a dialectal variant; vueso /ˈbweso/ shows the competing labial reinforcement.
